about: The goal is live and the morning check of 20 November has run. The person opens the standing goal and asks in the chat for two changes. The analyst drafts them, shows this change plan, and publishes version 2 of the dashboard when told to. Version 1 is the demo_run scorecard.
asked_in_the_chat: Add a signal for boil water notices in the last twelve months, under Water Quality and Contaminants, and make it a red flag
Change days sales outstanding: score 4 from 75 days
steps_the_analyst_shows: apply it to a draft of the scorecard
look for the data in what is connected
score all 300 projects on the draft
write the mitigation plans again where they change

signal.name: Boil water notices in the last twelve months
rule_1_to_4: Two or three in twelve months
More than three in twelve months

source.name: Operations data hub
source.how: The closest fields found for the description; shown for you to confirm

when_published: All 300 projects are scored again. The dashboard becomes version 2 and says why.
Version 1 stays in the version list of the dashboard.
The mitigation plans are written again for 25 sites.
Nobody is alerted. The scores move because the scoring changed, not because something happened at a site.
The next morning check uses the new scoring.
other_requests_the_chat_understands: add a factor, with a first signal
change how much a factor counts
drop or put back a signal or a factor
make a signal a red flag, or take the flag off
take the thresholds of a figure from history
set all three thresholds of a figure
take the higher of the two halves, or their average
refused: thresholds that are out of order
a rule that follows a regulatory or permit limit
a signal that is already on the scorecard
a request it cannot read: it gives examples instead of guessing
